units.upstream: $${i} should equal process.argv[${i}] (one test per process.argv entry)
units.api: For every index i of process.argv (bun test: typically [bunExecutablePath, testFilePath]), `echo $${{raw: i}}` (i.e. `echo $0`, `echo $1`, ...) run through Bun.$ prints process.argv[i] + "\n" with exitCode 0: inside Bun.$ the positional parameters $0..$9 are the host process argv.
units.note: the exact values depend on the host process argv, so the cases below only check structural properties (non-empty $0, $10 == $1 followed by "0", $2$2 == $2 twice)

cases.note: in Bun.$ $0 is process.argv[0] (the runtime executable path)
only single-digit positionals: "$10" parses as $1 followed by "0"
When process.argv[2] is unset, Bun 1.4.2 drops a quoted empty variable expansion ("$2" yields no argument), so the output is just "\n".

units.api:
Positionals (bun run of a .bun.sh script): `bun run <script.bun.sh> args...` executes the file with Bun's shell, where $0 is the script path as given and $1..$9 are the arguments; unset positionals expand to the empty string; only single-digit positionals exist, so `$10` is `$1` followed by a literal "0"; `$2$2` concatenates. Bun.$ itself takes no positional arguments (inside Bun.$ templates $N expands to process.argv[N]), so these standalone-script tests need a script-runner API with explicit argv. Assertion: `bun run fixtures/positionals.bun.sh a b c` where the script is `echo $0
echo $1
echo $2$2
` prints "<scriptPath>
a
bb
" (stdout.split("
") == [script, "a", "bb", ""]) and empty stderr.

Assertion: `bun run fixtures/positionals.bun.sh` (no args) prints "<scriptPath>


" (split == [script, "", "", ""]): missing positionals expand to empty, and `$2$2` of empty is empty; stderr empty.

Assertion: `bun run fixtures/positionals2.bun.sh a b c d e f g h i j k l` where the script echoes $0, $1, $2$2, $3 ... $9, $10 on separate lines prints lines [script, "a", "bb", "c", "d", "e", "f", "g", "h", "i", "a0", ""] ($10 is $1 + "0"; args beyond $9 are unreachable); stderr empty.
